{{recipe}}

'''Pepper steak''' is a dish where tender beef steaks are crusted with cracked peppercorns and then seared in a hot pan. A pan sauce can then be made of the meat drippings.
== Ingredients ==
* [[Cookbook:Salt#Types of salt|Kosher salt]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (24–32 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]]) [[Cookbook:Beef#Loin|beef tenderloin steaks]], 1 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] black [[Cookbook:Pepper|peppercorns]], cracked
* ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Cognac|cognac]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Cream|heavy cream]]
* ¼ cup unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], divided
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]

== Procedure ==
#Sprinkle steaks on both sides liberally with kosher salt. Press peppercorns into both sides of each steak. Let sit for 30 minutes or until room temperature.
#Melt 1 tbsp butter with oil in a large stainless steel [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] over medium high heat. Add steaks and cook 5 minutes per side for medium rare, 6 for medium, and 7 for well done. Remove from pan and keep warm.
#Raise heat in pan to high. Turn off the heat, then [[Cookbook:Deglazing|deglaze]] pan with cognac. Carefully ignite with a firestick or kitchen lighter, then swirl the pan until flames die.
#Put heat to medium and whisk continuously to remove fond. Bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] and cook until liquid has reduced by half.
#[[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] in cream. Bring to a boil and cook until liquid has reduced to ⅓ cup.
#Slowly whisk in butter, 1 tbsp at a time. Spoon sauce over steaks and serve warm.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Don't even think about using a nonstick pan. You can't build a pan sauce in a nonstick skillet.
* If you don't want to ignite the cognac, you do not have to. It just makes a performance that makes people stare at you with amazement.

== Warnings ==

* If you do choose to ignite, remember to keep a lid, in case things get out of hand, and a fire extinguisher, in case something bad happens and you need it.
